modules.name: project-memory
modules.trigger: Always when enabled.
modules.exitSignal: The memory layout is canonical and conflict-free, or a trivial legacy-only task explicitly deferred migration; relevant current project memory was read and meaningful new knowledge was recorded.
evidence: Current-task trace or report identifies the memory layout state and the relevant canonical .sdlc/memory or deferred legacy project-memory files inspected.
A legacy-only project-memory directory was migrated intact for non-trivial work; trivial work may read it only when migration is explicitly deferred and reported.
A dual-path or linked-path conflict blocked progress without merging, following, or deleting data.
Any durable decision, correction, constraint, architecture change, or active-context change is reflected in .sdlc/memory files.

modules.name: project-standards
modules.trigger: Always when enabled.
modules.exitSignal: Repository-specific engineering and delivery rules are identified.
evidence: Current-task trace or report identifies the standards file inspected, or establishes that none exists.
Inferred commands and conventions are tied to inspectable repository files when standards are absent.

modules.name: change-contract
modules.trigger: Always when enabled to establish the change contract.
modules.exitSignal: Repository findings, outcome, acceptance criteria, non-goals, impact, PR boundary, and costly open decisions are clear at the rigor required by the change.
evidence: For a Significant existing-codebase change, a concise discovery brief identifies inspected evidence, existing decisions and patterns, integration points, relevant constraints, facts, assumptions, and unknowns before clarification.
An inspectable specification, plan, issue, conversation decision, or change brief states the outcome, acceptance criteria, non-goals, affected surfaces, coherent boundary, and unresolved decisions.
For user-facing changes, the target user and benefit are clear; scenarios and success metrics are included when they materially define behavior or success.

modules.name: prd
modules.trigger: A new project, a new user-facing or product-facing feature, or a Significant internal feature introduces a new capability.
modules.exitSignal: A durable, identifiable, current PRD is complete, explicitly approved, and traceable through numbered requirements and acceptance criteria.
evidence: The artifact identifies itself with PRD frontmatter containing a stable ID, approved status, and positive version.

The PRD defines problem, target users and benefit, outcome, goals, non-goals, scenarios, numbered functional requirements and acceptance criteria, data and authority concerns, constraints, conditional success measures, open decisions, and approval evidence.
Every applicable change-contract acceptance criterion maps to a numbered PRD AC identifier or is explicitly superseded with developer approval.
No approval-blocking decision remains unresolved, and planning can map implementation and verification to FR and AC identifiers.

modules.name: debugging
modules.trigger: A bug or unexplained failure is in scope.
modules.exitSignal: The root cause is supported by reproduction and a tested hypothesis.
evidence: A deterministic reproduction or current diagnostic evidence localizes the failure.
A falsifiable root-cause hypothesis was tested, and regression sensitivity is demonstrated or its limitation is explicit.

modules.name: planning
modules.trigger: The change is Standard or Significant.
modules.exitSignal: A current proportional implementation and verification plan exists, including dependency-aware execution for Significant work.
evidence: An inspectable current plan covers approach, affected files, sequencing, scope, verification, risk, and deferred work.
The plan still matches the current change contract, authoritative design, and repository state.
When a PRD is selected, the plan identifies its path, ID, approved version, and maps tasks and verification to FR and AC identifiers.
A Significant plan identifies task prerequisites, consumed and produced interfaces, conservative parallel groups, and later integration work.

modules.name: accessibility-browser
modules.trigger: A change creates or modifies rendered web or mobile UI, user interaction behavior, responsive layout, navigation or focus behavior, accessibility semantics, or browser-only runtime behavior.
modules.exitSignal: Every affected user flow has current browser or app-runtime evidence at relevant viewport and input modes, applicable accessibility checks pass, and any unresolved usability or accessibility limitation is explicit.
evidence: An affected-flow inventory maps changed acceptance criteria to pages, screens, interaction states, viewport classes, and relevant input modes.
Current runtime evidence exercises each changed flow through the real rendered interface, including applicable loading, empty, error, disabled, validation, and success states.
Automated accessibility results cover affected rendered surfaces, and manual evidence covers applicable assistive input, focus, names, announcements, reflow, and motion behavior.
Responsive evidence names tested viewport classes and records overflow, clipping, target size, orientation, and content-reflow outcomes.
Findings identify severity, affected flow, reproduction, and disposition, with accepted limitations visible in final risk and handoff evidence.

modules.name: performance-concurrency
modules.trigger: A change has an explicit latency, throughput, capacity, or resource objective; modifies an evidenced hot path; or introduces or changes concurrency, parallel work, batching, caching, streaming, queueing, rate control, or shared mutable state.
modules.exitSignal: The relevant budget or baseline is explicit, representative current measurements meet it without correctness, contention, or resource regressions, and remaining capacity limits or measurement uncertainty are disclosed.
evidence: A measurable hypothesis identifies the operation, workload, baseline or budget, metric, environment, and expected direction or threshold.
Before-and-after measurements use the same representative workload and method, include repetitions that expose variance, and identify material environmental limitations.
Concurrency evidence covers applicable race, ordering, cancellation, timeout, retry, duplicate work, deadlock, starvation, backpressure, and shared-state behavior.
Resource evidence reports applicable CPU, memory, I/O, network, connection, queue-depth, or cache metrics, including relevant warm and cold conditions.
Tests or invariants demonstrate correctness at the measured load, and evidence records the current revision and measurement source.

modules.name: observability
modules.trigger: A change adds, removes, or modifies logs, metrics, traces, dashboards, or alerts; introduces or changes a service, queue, scheduled-job, or other asynchronous production boundary; or has an accepted requirement for new diagnostic or operational signals.
modules.exitSignal: Each affected production boundary and failure mode has current, queryable, privacy-safe diagnostic evidence with defined meaning and bounded cardinality or volume; applicable alerts have actionable thresholds and validated routing or are explicitly deferred as missing evidence.
evidence: A signal map ties affected boundaries and important failure modes to named signals and states the diagnostic question each answers.
Current output or deterministic telemetry tests prove names, fields, units, status, correlation, and failure classification at the real instrumentation boundary.
Privacy evidence shows that secrets, credentials, sensitive payloads, and unnecessary personal data are excluded or transformed according to project policy.
Metric and attribute cardinality is reviewed, and material log or trace volume, sampling, and retention implications are bounded.
Changed alerts identify destination or owner, threshold, window, severity, response, and validated fire and no-fire behavior.
Signal changes preserve or explicitly migrate dashboards, alerts, queries, and other consumers.

modules.name: api-compatibility
modules.trigger: A change adds, removes, or modifies a consumer-visible request, response, command, event, schema, serialization, error, SDK, generated-client, or versioning contract, including behavior observable by an independently deployed or external consumer.
modules.exitSignal: Affected consumers and contract deltas are explicit; compatible and breaking changes are classified; required versioning, deprecation, generated artifacts, and mixed-version behavior are implemented; and current contract plus representative consumer evidence passes.
evidence: A before-and-after contract delta identifies affected operations, fields, types, defaults, validation, side effects, ordering, errors, and version identifiers.
A consumer inventory names internal, external, generated, and independently deployed consumers, or records bounded evidence that none exist.
Each delta is classified as compatible, conditionally compatible, or breaking for those consumers, including relevant serialization differences.
Current contract tests cover success and error shapes, and representative old and new consumer or provider combinations prove the required compatibility window.
Applicable generated clients, schemas, documentation, examples, fixtures, and compatibility baselines are regenerated from maintained sources and checked for drift.
Breaking changes have explicit approval, versioning, transition guidance, and rollout sequencing.

modules.name: data-migration
modules.trigger: A change transforms, backfills, moves, reinterprets, or deletes durable production data; changes a production schema in a way that requires old and new application or schema versions to coexist; or introduces a migration whose failure could leave persistent state partial or invalid.
modules.exitSignal: The expand, backfill, switch, and contract sequence is explicit; current production-like rehearsal proves integrity, idempotency or resumability, mixed-version safety, and failure handling; rollback is tested where possible, otherwise a tested mitigation and irreversibility statement are present.
evidence: A migration inventory identifies source and target representations, volume and shape assumptions, invariants, ownership, retention, and destructive or irreversible steps.
The sequence separates compatible expand, backfill, verification, consumer switch, and destructive contract stages with gates and prerequisites.
Backfill evidence covers applicable batching, checkpoints, idempotency, resume, live writes, error quarantine, and bounded resource use.
Integrity evidence reconciles counts and domain invariants, samples transformed records, detects partial state, and defines acceptance thresholds.
A production-like rehearsal records duration, load, failures, mixed-version compatibility, and post-migration validation.
Rollback evidence restores code, schema, and data where reversible; otherwise a tested mitigation and irreversibility statement are explicit.

modules.name: dependency-supply-chain
modules.trigger: A change adds, removes, replaces, updates, pins, vendors, generates, downloads, or changes the resolution or execution of a third-party dependency, package manager, registry, lockfile, build plugin, action, container base, or fetched build artifact.
modules.exitSignal: Each changed third-party component is necessary, resolves reproducibly from an approved provenance, has current advisory and license assessment, has reviewed transitive and build-script impact, and passes focused compatibility plus repository verification with residual risk disclosed.
evidence: A dependency delta identifies direct and transitive additions, removals, versions, sources, integrity data, lockfile changes, scripts or plugins, and runtime or build-time placement.
A necessity record explains why platform, standard-library, or current dependency capabilities cannot meet the accepted outcome.
Provenance evidence identifies configured source, available publisher or owner, integrity mechanism, release identity, and vendored or generated origin.

Current advisory and maintenance evidence records the approved source, source identity, result time or advisory-database identity, severity disposition, supported versions, and signs of abandonment or compromise; evidence becomes stale after advisory-database changes unless its identity still matches.
License evidence identifies declared licenses and compatibility with project policy, escalating ambiguity instead of guessing.
Focused tests cover changed behavior, and clean or frozen restore evidence proves reproducibility and detects unexpected artifacts or scripts where supported.
High-risk updates include release-guidance review, transitive diff, rollback, and residual-risk disclosure without automatic network, install, update, or publication actions.

modules.name: tdd
modules.trigger: New behavior or a bug fix changes executable behavior.
modules.exitSignal: Each changed behavior has inspectable red-before-green evidence against real behavior, followed by minimal green and safe refactor, or a valid narrow technical exception.
evidence: A focused test was written before production implementation and failed for the expected missing or defective behavior.
The minimum implementation made the focused test pass, and any refactor preserved the green state.
Tests exercise real behavior, with mocks limited to genuine external seams.
Generated output, configuration-only behavior, or unsafe reproduction exceptions identify the category, technical reason, and strongest safe alternative evidence.

modules.name: implementation
modules.trigger: Code or configuration changes are required.
modules.exitSignal: The minimum complete implementation and authoritative design match the current contract through verified, safe, reversible slices.
evidence: The slice sequence identifies each increment's outcome, scope, verification checkpoint, exposure strategy, and reversal path.
Each completed slice left the repository coherent and has fresh affected checks tied to its resulting work product.

The inspectable final diff implements every acceptance criterion within the agreed boundary, including necessary tests, documentation, migrations, configuration, compatibility handling, and generated artifacts.

Any accepted requirement, public-contract, or architecture change discovered during implementation is synchronized to the PRD and renewed approval when selected, authoritative design, project memory when selected, plan, and dependent evidence.

modules.name: testing
modules.trigger: Behavior, bug, refactor, tests, or non-trivial verification are in scope.
modules.exitSignal: Acceptance evidence is fresh and test sensitivity is known.
evidence: Fresh command or CI results are tied to the current implementation revision and cover the relevant acceptance criteria.
When a PRD is selected, acceptance evidence is traceable to every approved AC identifier.
Bug regression sensitivity is demonstrated, or a technical limitation and credible alternative evidence are explicit.

modules.name: security-auth
modules.trigger: External input, stored or sensitive data, network access, identity, permissions, secrets, dependencies, or user-visible output are affected.
modules.exitSignal: Applicable security, authentication, and authorization risks are mitigated or disclosed.
evidence: A current analysis identifies applicable trust, input, auth, data, secret, dependency, and abuse risks for the actual diff.
Mitigations, tests, and any accepted residual risk are inspectable and scope-aligned.

modules.name: operational-readiness
modules.trigger: Production data, public contracts, runtime or deployment configuration, infrastructure, background processing, or rollout are affected.
modules.exitSignal: Reversibility, compatibility, rollout, operational signals, and post-change checks are credible.
evidence: A current plan defines compatibility sequencing, rollout, rollback or mitigation, measurable signals, and post-change validation.
Required rehearsal, restore, dry-run, or production-like evidence is current and inspectable.

modules.name: review
modules.trigger: Always before completion when enabled.
modules.exitSignal: Risk-scaled perspectives reviewed the current final diff and findings were triaged.
evidence: Review output identifies the actual final diff or revision, perspectives used, actionable findings, and confidence.
Relevant findings are resolved or disclosed, and affected checks were rerun after fixes.

modules.name: pr-handoff
modules.trigger: Always before completion when enabled to prepare PR handoff.
modules.exitSignal: Final repository state and a human-readable handoff support a readiness decision.
evidence: Current repository status and complete diff were inspected against the coherent boundary.

The handoff maps outcome, PRD path/ID/version and delivered FR/AC identifiers when selected, scope, acceptance evidence, review, compatibility, rollout or rollback, limitations, deferred work, and risk.

modules.name: continuous-improvement
modules.trigger: A task produces a correction, repeated merge step, recurring review finding or coverage gap, explicit learning request, or an SDLC core upgrade changes core responsibilities.
modules.exitSignal: Learning signals and upgrade-driven extension overlap were classified and routed, recorded, proposed, accepted, rejected, or proposed for supersession with rationale.
evidence: Every qualifying signal is matched to existing configuration, standards, memory, core behavior, or a sanitized candidate.
No extension is active without inspectable validation and explicit developer approval.
